newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says repulses big rebel attack in north.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says repulses big rebel attack in north.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops have repulsed a big attack by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels on government forward positions in the island's northeast, a military spokesman said on Thursday.

Brigadier Sarath Munasinghe said at least 60 rebels were killed in the attack late Wednesday near Nedunkeni, which was captured by the army in the initial days of "Operation Jayasikuru", or "Sure of Victory", that was launched in May to open a strategic highway.
"Seventeen bodies of the rebels along with arms and ammunition have been recovered by ground troops. We believe at least 100 rebels were wounded," Munasinghe told a news conference in Colombo.
"We have lost one officer and 16 soldiers. Two officers and 25 soldiers were wounded," he said, adding that fighting continued for more than three hours.
An LTTE spokesman in London was not immediately available for comment.

The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
Military officials said Wednesday's rebel attack was one of the biggest since they launched two counter-attacks on troops involved in Operation Jayasikuru last month.

Scores of soldiers and rebels were killed in the previous attacks at Thandikulam and Periyamadu, north of the government-held town of Vavuniya, which lies some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
Munasinghe said he estimated that the army was fighting some 4,000 rebels in the north.
He said food and refugee ships to the northern Jaffna peninsula would be escorted by the Sri Lankan navy after the rebels attacked two vessels in the area earlier this month and abducted their crew.
The rebels said on Tuesday they would attack ships in the seas off Jaffna because they carried supplies to the Sri Lankan military.
"Under these conditions, the LTTE has no option but to regard these military servicing Sri Lankan vessels as legitimate military targets," the rebels said in a statement from their London office.
"This shows the true colours of LTTE," Munasinghe said. "They want to starve the people of Jaffna."
All food and other essential supplies to Jaffna are transported by sea or air because there is no road linking the peninsula with the rest of the island.
Shipping lines stopped their services after the rebel attacks, demanding protection.
"Our navy will go through any barriers and we will somehow take food to Jaffna. Let LTTE make any statement, we are not bothered," Munasinghe said.
He said refugee ships would also be escorted by the U.N. High Commission for Refugees.
Sri Lanka is resettling hundreds of thousands of people in Jaffna who fled south to the brush jungles of the Wanni when the army captured the northern peninsula last year.
